analysis: Examined base text of ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift (lines 2231-3080) and the visible patch excerpt. The visible head changes add two operations hooks, `stopsAsked` and `serveUnlessStopped` (default nil/nil, so default behaviour is unchanged). They also thread a `stopsBefore:` parameter into `provision(...)`. The one call-site change I could see passes `stopsBefore: nil` on the refusal path. This is a local CLI onboarding/UX flow that sits outside the TB-002 coordinator WebSocket path. It touches the A-018 serving-availability and cluster start/stop lifecycle only through the intended stop-race fix (a stop that took the lock first is not undone). I found no change to authentication, attestation, encryption, cache storage (T-041), the TB-012 hold socket, the TB-013 installer download, or TB-014 root commands in the supplied excerpt. The patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false) and the head text was not supplied. Unseen changes at head lines about 2901-3209 and 3316-3539 are therefore not reviewed. They include the `provision` signature change, the `serveUnlessStopped` implementation, the stop-count read, and the `stopsBefore` handling. Integration should check that: (1) the live `serveUnlessStopped` actually takes the leader's lock and compares the stop count, and that a nil stop count fails open or closed as intended; (2) the `stopsBefore` value is captured before any user prompts; (3) the stop path still stops serving on both Macs; (4) no new privileged execution (`runAsAdministrator`/`setUpPortWithSudo` use) or untrusted-input path was added in the unseen head hunks. No concrete regression is supported by the visible evidence.
